name: Clonk
tagline: An AI product at clonk.ai whose public pitch is thin enough that we will not pretend to know its exact shape yet.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Full disclosure: we have not verified what Clonk actually does, so treat this entry as a placeholder with a build attached rather than a review. Products in this shape, a hosted wrapper around a general model with a nicer interface and some memory of your files, are the single most one-shottable category there is, and a coding agent will get you a working local version in an evening. What you cannot one-shot is whatever specific harness, eval work, or data plumbing sits underneath, and that is exactly the part a landing page never shows. So the honest verdict is kinda: the visible surface is cheap to rebuild, the invisible part is unknown. If the product turns out to lean on proprietary data or a fine-tuned model rather than a prompt and a decent UI, this moves to no.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app that chats with an OpenAI-compatible model, remembers conversations in SQLite, and can pull in your own local files as context.
requirements: An API key for an OpenAI-compatible model provider
Somewhere to run it, localhost is fine
whatYouLose: Whatever the hosted product does that its marketing copy does not spell out, which may be the actual value
Model routing and cost control done by someone else, so your bill is now your problem
Mobile access, unless you feel like deploying and locking it down yourself
Any team features: sharing, permissions, seats, audit trails
Someone to blame when the provider API changes shape
moatNotes: Execution polish is the only moat we can see from outside. If there is a real model or data asset under the hood, it is not advertised loudly enough to score.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a chat box that already works beats a chat box you have to maintain, and most buyers are not paying for the model, they are paying for not thinking about keys, quotas, retries, and the ten small UI decisions that make an assistant feel usable at 11pm. A local clone gets you the loop, not the calm. It also gets you a bill that scales with your curiosity instead of a flat number you can budget.
notes: Entry drafted from a submission with an unverified product scope, so the verdict is provisional and will move once someone actually reads the docs.
prompt:
Build a local, single-user AI assistant workspace. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non negotiable:
- Next.js 15 with the App Router and TypeScript
- Tailwind CSS for styling, no component library
- SQLite via better-sqlite3 for storage, file at ./data/app.db
- Model access through any OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint

Environment, read from .env.local and nothing else:
- OPENAI_API_KEY
- OPENAI_BASE_URL (default https://api.openai.com/v1)
- MODEL (default gpt-4o-mini)
- WORKSPACE_DIR, an absolute path to a folder of my own text files

Features in scope:
1. Chat UI with streaming token output, markdown rendering, and code blocks with a copy button.
2. Conversation list in a left sidebar: create, rename, delete. All messages persisted in SQLite.
3. A context panel that lists text files found under WORKSPACE_DIR (recurse, allow .md .txt .json .ts .py, skip node_modules and dotfiles). I can check files to attach; attached file contents get inlined into the system prompt with a total character budget of 60000 and a clear warning in the UI when the budget is exceeded.
4. An editable system prompt per conversation, stored with the conversation.
5. Token and cost estimate per message, based on a hardcoded price table in one config file. Rough is fine, label it as rough.
6. Full text search across stored messages using SQLite FTS5.

Explicitly out of scope: auth, multi user, embeddings, vector search, RAG chunking, file uploads, agents that write to disk, and any analytics.

Safety rails: never read outside WORKSPACE_DIR, resolve and validate paths, and refuse symlinks that escape it.

Deliverables: working app, npm run dev on port 3000, a .env.local.example, a seeded empty database created on first run, and a README with setup in under ten lines. Handle API errors and rate limits visibly in the UI instead of failing silently.
